# Fitting Generalized Extreme Value Distribution to Asheville Precipitation

### Data Preparation and Package Import 

``` {r initialization}
# Package Import
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(evd)
library(extRemes)

# Data Import
asheville_df <- read.csv("../data/ghcn_roi_daily_data/Asheville.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Data cleaning
## Basic
asheville_df <- asheville_df %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>% # put date in date data format
  filter(!is.na(precipitation)) # Remove any missing precip entries
## Add block maxima (1-year maximum precipitation)
annual_max <- asheville_df %>%
  mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarize(annual_max_precip = max(precipitation, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_days = sum(!is.na(precipitation)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(is.finite(annual_max_precip))
## Check on resulting data:
print(head(annual_max))
cat("Number of years available:", nrow(annual_max), "\n")
ggplot(annual_max, aes(x = annual_max_precip)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 11) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of annual maxima (daily precipitation)", x = "Annual max (mm)", y = "Count")
```

``` {r fitting-GEV-one-day-periods}
# Set random seed for MLE
set.seed(5845)

# evd::fgev uses parameterization (location = mu, scale = sigma > 0, shape = xi)
# Starting values are important; fgev can compute defaults but we pick sensible starts.
x <- annual_max$annual_max_precip

# try a fit with evd
gev_fit_evd <- tryCatch(
  fgev(x, std.err = TRUE),
  error = function(e) {
    message("evd::fgev failed with error: ", e$message, "\nAttempting with initial estimates.")
    # sensible initials: location = mean, log(scale)=log(sd), shape small (0.1)
    fgev(x, start = list(loc = mean(x), scale = sd(x), shape = 0.1), std.err = TRUE)
  }
)

summary(gev_fit_evd)
print(gev_fit_evd$std.err)
# Grab estimates and standard errors
est_evd <- gev_fit_evd$estimate
se_evd  <- gev_fit_evd$std.err # works to get SEs
cat("\nEVD (fgev) estimates:\n")
print(data.frame(parameter = c("loc","scale","shape"), estimate = est_evd, se = se_evd))

# Compute return levels using evd::qgev:
# Return period T years => non-exceedance prob p = 1 - 1/T for annual maxima
return_periods <- c(20, 50, 100, 114, 500)
pvals <- 1 - 1/return_periods
rls_evd <- sapply(pvals, function(p) qgev(p, loc = est_evd["loc"], scale = est_evd["scale"], shape = est_evd["shape"]))
rl_df <- data.frame(return_period = return_periods, return_level = rls_evd)
print(rl_df)
```


```{r return-level-calculation}
# RETURN LEVELS

# Parameters for Gumbel fit
mu_gumbel <- 67.02
sigma_gumbel <- 18.81

# Desired return periods (years)
return_periods <- c(5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000)

# Compute return levels
return_levels <- mu_gumbel - sigma_gumbel * log( -log(1 - 1/return_periods) )

# Combine into a data frame
gev_rl_df <- data.frame(
  ReturnPeriod_years = return_periods,
  ReturnLevel_mm = return_levels
)

print(gev_rl_df)

# HELENE
# Example: return period for a level x = 146.8 mm
x_level <- 146.8

T_x <- 1 / (1 - exp( -exp( -(x_level - mu_gumbel)/sigma_gumbel ) ))

cat("Return period for", x_level, "mm =", round(T_x, 1), "years\n")
```

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height=5.25}
#-----EMPIRICAL POINTS FOR PLOT-------------
# Sort annual maxima in descending order
annual_max_sorted <- annual_max %>%
  arrange(desc(annual_max_precip)) %>%
  mutate(rank = row_number(),
         ReturnPeriod_years = n() / rank,  # T = N/i, for annual maxima
         ReturnLevel_mm = annual_max_precip)
empirical_df <- annual_max_sorted

#------- SPECIAL POINT FOR HURRICANE HELENE RETURN PERIOD -------------------
x_level <- 146.8
special_T_years <- 1 / (1 - exp( -exp( -(x_level - mu_gumbel)/sigma_gumbel ) ))

special_point <- data.frame(
  ReturnPeriod_years = special_T_years,
  ReturnLevel_mm = x_level
)

#-------- 95% CONFIDENCE INTERVAL FORMULATION --------------------------------
se_mu <- 5.0    # example: replace with real value from gev_fit_evd$std.err
se_sigma <- 2.0 # example

# Return periods
return_periods <- c(5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000)
k_T <- -log(1 - 1/return_periods)

# Compute return levels
return_levels <- mu_gumbel - sigma_gumbel * log(k_T)

# Delta method standard errors
se_rl <- sqrt(se_mu^2 + (log(k_T) * se_sigma)^2)

# 95% CI
lower_ci <- return_levels - 1.96 * se_rl
upper_ci <- return_levels + 1.96 * se_rl

# Combine into data frame for plotting
gev_rl_ci_df <- data.frame(
  ReturnPeriod_years = return_periods,
  ReturnLevel_mm = return_levels,
  Lower_CI = lower_ci,
  Upper_CI = upper_ci
)

#-------- PLOT CALL ----------------------------------------------------------
ggplot() +
  # 95% CI ribbon
  geom_ribbon(data = gev_rl_ci_df,
              aes(x = ReturnPeriod_years, ymin = Lower_CI, ymax = Upper_CI),
              fill = "lightblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  # Gumbel fit line
  geom_line(data = gev_rl_ci_df, aes(x = ReturnPeriod_years, y = ReturnLevel_mm),
            color = "cyan4", size = 1) +
  # Empirical annual maxima
  geom_point(data = empirical_df, aes(x = ReturnPeriod_years, y = ReturnLevel_mm),
             color = "red3", size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Special labeled point
  geom_point(data = special_point, aes(x = ReturnPeriod_years, y = ReturnLevel_mm),
             color = "darkgreen", size = 4) +
  geom_text(data = special_point,
            aes(x = ReturnPeriod_years, y = ReturnLevel_mm,
                label = paste0("(", round(ReturnPeriod_years,1), " yr, ", ReturnLevel_mm, " mm)")),
            vjust = -1.5, hjust = 0.5, color = "darkgreen", fontface = "bold",
            size = 3.5) +
  # Log scale x-axis
  scale_x_log10(
    limits = c(5, max(c(gev_rl_ci_df$ReturnPeriod_years, empirical_df$ReturnPeriod_years))),
    breaks = c(5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000),
    labels = c(5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Return Level vs Return Period (Empirical + Gumbel Fit)",
    subtitle = "Empirical annual maxima vs Gumbel return levels with 95% CI",
    x = "Return Period (years, log scale)",
    y = "Return Level (mm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```
